page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highmem-80 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the n4d family. It features 80 dedicated virtual CPUs and 640.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This high memory density positions the server within the memory-optimized category, designed for workloads requiring substantial RAM allocations relative to compute resources.

The instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage options. Additionally, it does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The lack of local NVMe drives and hardware accelerators represents a clear tradeoff, focusing the resource profile entirely on memory capacity and dedicated CPU execution.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n4d-highmem-80 offers a dense allocation of memory per dedicated core, reducing the need to provision excess compute resources merely to obtain sufficient RAM. This resource distribution is appropriate for memory-intensive workloads such as large-scale databases, in-memory caching layers, enterprise applications, and data processing pipelines that do not require GPU acceleration or local scratch disks.
